messages:
ryan: Heads-up — we need to finalize the GPU spot procurement playbook for the new EU region rollout. Eviction patterns look different there.

maria: Agreed. Quick summary: capacity-optimized pools gave us lower eviction rate last month but higher baseline cost. Price-optimized saved money but had spikes in interruptions.

kevin: Can we run a mixed strategy? e.g., primary capacity-optimized allocation + a small price-optimized chase pool for extra throughput during low-price windows.

anika: That was my proposal in the doc. Suggested ratios: 70/20/10 (reserved/dedicated/spot-mix) for production-critical jobs, but for batch training push: 40 reserved / 60 mixed-spot.

ryan: For inference fleets we must keep latency SLAs. So reserved or Dedicated first, then capacity-optimized spot as failover to avoid frequent evictions.

maria: Implementation notes: set ASG allocationStrategy to `capacity-optimized` for the main pool. For chase pool use `price-optimized` with a dynamic maxPrice that follows a 5% buffer above median price.

kevin: Important: do NOT set maxPrice to on-demand for chase pools — that defeats the point. Use a sliding window: if current spot price < targetThreshold && evictionRate < 0.5% then scale chase pool.

anika: Also add region-aware fallbacks: prefer same AZ capacity-optimized, then cross-AZ capacity-optimized, then cross-region price-optimized as last resort. Document the fallback priority in the autoscaler.

spot-bot: [alert] AWS Spot: 2-minute termination notice detected in eu-west-2 for instance i-0abcd1234.

ryan: Nice — sounds like we need termination handlers wired to checkpointing. For training we must push checkpoints to S3 and mark resume points in Dynamo/metadata store. For serving, drain connections and shift traffic to Dedicated instances first.

maria: K8s details: use node-termination-handler + PDBs + PodDisruption budgets tuned to prefer graceful drains. Also use taints for capacity-optimized nodes so low-priority pods can be evicted to chase pool.

kevin: Bidding strategy: don't try to outbid market. Instead, use a lookback predictor for spot price spikes (30m rolling median + volatility multiplier). Auto-scale triggers should check both price and eviction trend.

anika: For the chase pool, we should implement short-lived instances and fast-preemption workloads only. Add tagging to identify ephemeral vs sticky caches so we don't lose hot KV.

ryan: Operational play: run a daily job that simulates a 10% capacity loss and measure failover time to Dedicated and chase pools. Target recovery < 90s for critical inference routes.

maria: Cost metric: track effective $/GPU-hour including wasted time from evictions (i.e., restart overhead). Optimize for minimized total $/useful-work, not just hourly VM price.

kevin: One more: prefer newer instance types in capacity-optimized pools (they have larger pools in the region) but keep a compatibility matrix so models that need large memory go to specific SKUs.

anika: I'll update the playbook with concrete ASG/allocator config and a CLI command to toggle chase pool thresholds.

ryan: Great. Action items: Anika updates playbook, Maria adds metrics & dashboards, Kevin writes the price predictor stub, I'll schedule the chaos simulation. We'll reconvene tomorrow at 10:30am. :thumbsup:

maria: Copy that. Adding TODOs to the infra board. :white_check_mark:

kevin: I'll start a small POC in eu-west-2 with a 30/10 chase config and send results by EOD.

spot-bot: [info] Created ticket INFRA-981: "EU spot chase pool POC" assigned to kevin.
